_comment: Day-to-day inbound, as it actually arrives. Names here are ROLES, not colleagues — the committed starter set must not carry real people. Ground the real ones in data/scenarios/, which is gitignored.

given.subject: can you approve the PR today?

cases.why: someone is blocked until he moves — this is the case that must never be missed
cases.source: the ask he gets most: a PR waiting on his approval

given.subject: FYI - release notes for sprint 42, no action needed

cases.why: an FYI that buzzes his phone is the noise he complained about

given.subject: FYI on the release — but can you approve the hotfix by EOD?

cases.why: the FYI prefix is a habit, not a classification — the ask is what he is on the hook for

given.subject: mentioned you in Daily deployment slot

cases.why: being named is not being asked — worth knowing, not worth stopping for

given.subject: Automated: deployment to the sit environment succeeded

cases.why: a bot cannot be waiting on him; treating it as an ask is pure noise

given.subject: Quick one
given.preview: Hi Arun, hope you are doing well. Could you review the vessel ETA validation change before standup?

cases.why: quoting the greeting is what made previews feel like padding — he needs the sentence that asks

given.subject: we are blocked on your sign-off for the booking fix

cases.why: 'blocked' plus 'your' is the phrasing people actually use when they are waiting

given.subject: Weekly newsletter: platform updates and announcements

cases.why: broadcast mail outnumbers real asks; one false positive here trains him to ignore the channel
